title: The best Dialpad alternatives in 2026
summary: The best Dialpad alternatives for outbound sales in 2026, ranked. Artisan runs calling inside one AI-driven system, plus Nooks, Salesfinity, Koncert and more.
body_markdown:
The best Dialpad alternative for outbound sales is Artisan, because it puts calling inside one AI-driven outbound system instead of a broad communications suite. Calls become steps in an AI-run sequence, Ava does the prospecting around them, and pricing is usage-based. For dedicated parallel-dial floors, Nooks and Salesfinity go wider.

## Why do teams look for a Dialpad alternative?


Dialpad is a strong AI-native communications suite. It runs voice, video meetings, and a contact center with real-time transcription and coaching, priced per seat by tier per its pricing page. The catch for outbound sales is breadth. Dialpad is built to be a whole company's phone system, so its center of gravity is internal comms and customer support, not prospecting. A sales tier gives reps AI-assisted calling, but the leads, the email steps, the sequencing, and the reply handling still live in separate tools. Teams whose day is outbound often want a dialer that is part of the prospecting motion, with faster dial modes and tighter number-reputation controls than a general communications platform prioritizes.


## How we chose


We ran four tests, weighted for outbound sales instead of unified communications:


-


The tool should cover more than dialing: sourcing, writing, dialing, and reply handling all count.


-


Calls that run as steps inside a sequence beat a standalone softphone.


-


Published pricing beats demo-gated quotes.


-


Number pooling, do-not-call (DNC) checks, calling-hours enforcement, and CRM owner mapping matter across a large team.


## What is the best overall Dialpad alternative?


### 1. Artisan: Calling inside one AI-run outbound system


Artisan is the strongest Dialpad alternative for outbound because it is a prospecting system that happens to dial, built around the outreach instead of the phone. An AI business development representative (BDR) named Ava sources leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals across over 200 countries, enriches them with waterfall email and phone data, writes personalized outreach, dials, handles replies from a knowledge base, and books meetings on reps' calendars. Calls are steps in the same multichannel sequence as email and social media.


The dialer is enterprise-grade. Power and parallel dialing reach up to three lines with AI answer detection, live talking points before the call connects, live transcription, auto-classified outcomes, an AI-drafted follow-up email, AI voicemail drop, and automatic area-code matching. Numbers are pooled at the org level with personal callback routing so a lead who calls back reaches the right rep. Compliance runs per lead, covering calling-hours enforcement, federal DNC checks, consent-aware recording, and carrier spam-reputation monitoring that protects a large team's connect rates.


Pricing is the argument. Artisan is usage-based, so you pay for the work Ava actually performs: qualifying, enriching, personalizing, and sending messages. Over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously.


**Best for:** outbound teams from startup to enterprise that want the whole motion in one system, with sales ops running Ava centrally for account executives (AEs) who never log in.


**Who should pick something else:** teams whose entire day is maximum-volume parallel calling may want a dedicated 5-to-10-line floor.


**Pricing:** usage-based, with a free trial and no platform fee. See[Artisan pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### 2. Nooks: The parallel-dialing call floor


Nooks is a leading choice in parallel dialing for teams whose motion is volume calling. It dials multiple lines at once with AI answer detection and runs a virtual salesfloor for live coaching. Nooks raised a $43M Series B. Pricing is demo-gated, reportedly around $4,000 to $5,000/user/year billed annually, the tradeoff for a dedicated floor. See[Artisan vs. Nooks](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-nooks) and[Nooks pricing and reviews](https://www.artisan.co/blog/nooks-pricing-and-reviews) .


**Best for:** teams of sales development representatives (SDRs) that do hundreds of dials a day as their core job. **Who should pick something else:** teams that also need lead sourcing, email, and reply handling in one tool. **Pricing:** demo-gated; reportedly ~$4,000 to $5,000/user/year, billed annually.


### 3. Salesfinity: Transparent parallel dialing


Salesfinity publishes its price where most parallel dialers hide it. It runs five lines at $149 or $349/user/month per its pricing page. For a team that wants a straightforward parallel floor without a sales cycle to learn the cost, it is an easy shortlist entry and a clean contrast with gated rivals.


**Best for:** teams that want a parallel dialer with pricing they can see up front.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need the surrounding outbound motion, not just faster dials.


**Pricing:** $149 / $349/user/month, five lines, per its pricing page.


### 4. Koncert: Multi-mode dialing


Koncert bundles several dialing modes, parallel, flow, and agent-assisted, so teams can shift call styles as campaigns change. It is outbound-sales oriented and includes number-reputation features. Pricing is public, a per-seat ladder from Click at $6 to AI Parallel at $99/user/month across five dialing modes.


**Best for:** teams that want to switch between parallel and single-line dialing in one tool.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want an AI to run the cadence around the calls.


**Pricing:** $6 to $99/user/month public ladder.


### 5. Kixie: Power dialing plus SMS for reps


Kixie is a rep-focused power dialer with local presence dialing, voicemail drop, and SMS, wired tightly into CRMs. It speeds up manual outbound calling without a parallel floor's complexity. Reps who live in the CRM and want faster single-line dialing tend to like it, and it is a lighter jump from Dialpad's sales tier. See[Kixie vs. JustCall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/kixie-vs-justcall-which-should-you-choose-in-2026) .


**Best for:** individual reps and small teams that want quick CRM-connected dialing.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need parallel lines or an AI running the surrounding cadence.


**Pricing:** per-seat tiers, per its pricing page.


### 6. Aircall: Support and inside teams


Aircall is a business phone system with call routing, interactive voice response (IVR), a shared number, and a large app marketplace. Like Dialpad, it aims to run a company's phones rather than the outbound motion. If you are leaving Dialpad for telephony reasons rather than outbound scope, Aircall is a close like-for-like. See[Artisan vs. Aircall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-aircall) .


**Best for:** support desks and inside teams that need reliable telephony and integrations.


**Who should pick something else:** outbound teams that want a dialer wired into prospecting.


**Pricing:** per-seat tiers, per its pricing page.


### 7. JustCall: Phone plus SMS for smaller teams


JustCall is a cloud phone and texting platform for small and medium-sized business (SMB) sales and support, with a sales dialer, SMS, and CRM integrations in one app. It is a lighter, cheaper alternative to Dialpad's full suite that keeps voice and text together. For a small team, it covers the basics without a big build.


**Best for:** small sales and support teams that want voice and SMS together.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need the AI to source and write, not just dial and text.


**Pricing:** per-seat tiers, per its pricing page.


## Stay with Dialpad if...


Keep Dialpad if you want one platform for a whole company's communications. If you need voice, video meetings, and a contact center with AI transcription baked in, Dialpad does that broad job well, and outbound sales is a slice of it. The alternatives above matter when calling is one part of a prospecting motion instead of one feature of a communications suite.


CookUnity shows the payoff of consolidation. Bruno Didier, CEO of CookUnity Business, reported roughly a $45 cost per lead across over 100,000 personalized emails with Ava running highly targeted outreach at a scale a human-only team could not reach. Calls were part of the same AI-driven motion, not a separate app.

See also[parallel vs. power vs. predictive dialer](https://www.artisan.co/blog/parallel-dialer-vs-power-dialer-vs-predictive-dialer-which-do-you-need) and[Artisan vs. Orum](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-orum) .


## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to Dialpad for outbound sales?


Artisan, if you want the dialer inside a system that also sources leads, writes outreach, and handles replies. Calls run as steps in an AI-driven sequence, priced by usage. If your team only needs a high-volume call floor, Nooks and Salesfinity are stronger single-purpose picks with multiple parallel lines.


### Is Dialpad good for outbound sales calling?


Dialpad is an AI-native communications suite built to run a company's voice, meetings, and contact center. Its sales tier adds AI-assisted calling, but prospecting is not its center of gravity. For a team whose day is outbound, the leads, sequences, and reply handling live in other tools, so a sales-native system where calls are cadence steps usually fits better.


### What is the best enterprise alternative to Dialpad?


For enterprise outbound, Artisan pairs a compliant dialer with central-ops deployment: pooled org-level numbers, CRM owner mapping so calls log to the right rep, automatic DNC and calling-hours enforcement, and SOC 2 Type II attestation. Pricing is usage-based, so cost follows the work Ava performs. For a global standalone call floor, Orum-class parallel dialers remain the specialist choice.


### How does Artisan's dialer pricing compare to Dialpad's?


Artisan is usage-based. You pay for the work Ava performs across qualifying, enriching, personalizing, and sending, and the dialer runs inside that same platform. Dialpad prices per seat by tier, with sales-focused tiers costing more per its pricing page. Confirm current tiers directly, since communications pricing changes often.


### Does Artisan do parallel dialing?


Yes, up to three lines with AI answer detection, run as steps inside multichannel campaigns. This covers most outbound teams. Nooks dials multiple lines in parallel and Salesfinity runs five, so a team whose entire motion is maximum-volume parallel calling may still prefer a dedicated floor.


### Can one tool replace Dialpad and my sequencer for sales?


For outbound, Artisan can. It runs email, social media outreach, and dialer call steps in one AI-driven sequence, with lead sourcing, enrichment, reply handling, and meeting booking in the same platform. This consolidates the dialer, the sequencer, and the data tools most teams stitch together. It is not a full company-wide communications suite with video meetings the way Dialpad is.


## The bottom line


Dialpad is a communications suite. If outbound sales is the job, the stronger move is a system that dials as one part of running the whole motion.[Artisan](https://www.artisan.co/) puts calling inside an AI-driven outbound engine, with Ava handling sourcing, writing, and follow-up around every call. For a pure parallel-dial floor, Nooks and Salesfinity stay the specialists. See how the[AI sales agent](https://www.artisan.co/ai-sales-agent) fits together.
